clue.text: Short couple following French sea bird

indicators.note: the cut-down synonym comes after the French word in the answer

parts.note: mer is French for sea

indicators.note: a short word is cut off, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to couple is to link

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher describes a pair of seabirds trailing behind a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a sea bird as one unit; 'sea' belongs with 'French', and 'bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small falcon, a bird of prey found across Europe and North America.

clue.text: Rebel male greeting Little Richard?

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
Rick is a short form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A rebellious man says hello to the rock-and-roll star Little Richard.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard looks like the singer, but here 'Little' just shortens the name Richard to RICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded person who refuses to conform, a rebel against convention.

clue.text: Passing water leaders swap places causing devastation

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word change places with each other

parts.note: passing water is urination

explanation.surface: Someone relieving themselves where they shouldn't causes widespread damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening U and R of URINATION gives RUINATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is the state of being ruined, wholesale destruction, which is what devastation means.

clue.text: I live with cross creature

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone admits they live with an angry animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry, but it is the letter X, shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat, an animal of the Alps and other high ranges.

clue.text: Before noon gets one cold beer containing drop of blackcurrant cordial

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: the beer word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of blackcurrant is used

explanation.surface: A morning drinker has a cold beer with a splash of blackcurrant cordial in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like the drink, which fits the blackcurrant, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial as an adjective means warm and friendly, as does amicable.

clue.text: Greek character flies over for horse

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: gnats are small flies

explanation.surface: A Greek man flies across the world to buy a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb but is the noun, insects, here GNATS, read backwards as STANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or semi-wild horse of the American West.

clue.text: Money yields initially exchanged for medicine

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words swap places with each other

parts.note: dough is slang for money
crops are the yields of a harvest

explanation.surface: Cash and harvests are traded for medical supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the D of DOUGH with the C of CROPS to get COUGH DROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cough drops are lozenges taken to soothe a sore throat, a mild over-the-counter remedy.

clue.text: Offered to cross line for bit of grass

indicators.note: the offered word spans across the line letter, holding it inside

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, to offer

explanation.surface: Someone offers to walk across a line to fetch a bit of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a single leaf of grass, one narrow piece of the lawn.

clue.text: Tiny me aroused hostility?

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and set into a new order

explanation.surface: A small person asks whether their anger has been stirred into hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is deep-seated ill will between enemies, a synonym of hostility.

clue.text: Comedian having way to stop heckle

indicators.note: the way abbreviation plugs the middle of the heckle word, like a stopper

parts.note: to jeer is to heckle, shout mockingly
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A comedian finds a way to stop being heckled.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was the court fool, a professional joker, which a comedian is today.

clue.text: Dumb little mammals consuming cool shrew's head

indicators.note: the mammals eat up the cooling word, taking it inside

parts.note: voles are small rodents
to ice is to cool

indicators.note: a head is at the front, so the first letter of shrew is taken

parts.note: the shrew's head is its first letter

explanation.surface: Speechless little creatures munch on a chilled shrew head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumb' looks like an insult for the mammals, but it is the definition, in its old sense of mute.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb in its old sense means unable to speak, mute, so without a voice.

clue.text: Remove weapons from leaders of uprising nationalist association requesting munitions

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, read in order

explanation.surface: Disarm the heads of a rebel nationalist group asking for arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To unarm is an old verb for disarming, taking weapons away from someone.

clue.text: Shout of king having row

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
an oar is used to row

explanation.surface: A king shouts in a row with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is rowing a boat, with an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar is a loud, deep shout, as of anger or laughter.

clue.text: At Mach ten flying team initially bond

indicators.note: flying around, the letters scatter into a new order
only the first letter of team is used

explanation.surface: A flying display team zooms past at ten times the speed of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An attachment is a bond of affection or a connecting link between things.

clue.text: Love light fragrance shimmering

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
pale means light in colour
a scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A light, loving perfume with a shimmer to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent describes the milky iridescence of an opal, colours that shimmer and shift.

clue.text: Lively takeaway in Ireland?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in Ireland a ... is a fish-and-chip shop, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: The Irish sense is informal; a takeaway is a shop selling cooked food to carry home.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper as an adjective is cheerful, and in Irish usage the noun names the local chip shop.

clue.text: Soldier rejected champagne brand with expression of surprise

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the brand name is read backwards

parts.note: Krug is a champagne house
ha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A soldier is surprised to have his champagne refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gurkha is a Nepalese soldier serving in the British or Indian army.

clue.text: Tree — lots of trees — in LA suburb

parts.note: the holly is a tree
a wood is a place with many trees

explanation.surface: A list of trees, apparently growing in a Los Angeles suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood is a district of Los Angeles, home of the American film industry.

clue.text: Footballer put off round goal

indicators.note: the postponing word goes round the goal word

parts.note: to defer is to put off
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer is put off as he runs round towards the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' suggests the net, but it is END, as in an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is a footballer who plays at the back, protecting his own goal.

clue.text: Hearts of men and nobles enlocked as one

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter or letters, taken from each word in turn

explanation.surface: Common men and nobles are bound together in unity.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles are E, N, BL and OC; 'and' is a word to mine too, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is French for all together, as a single unit.

clue.text: Daily story for credulous chap

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British term for a cleaning woman
a story can be a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A newspaper story written to fool a gullible man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in British English it is also a cleaner who comes in each day, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a fool, someone easily taken in.

clue.text: Sudden urge I am going to beat

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: Someone feels a sudden urge to hit something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' reads as strike, but it is the noun, a rhythmic beat.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden desire to act, a whim acted on without thought.

clue.text: Killer men CIA deployed

indicators.note: agents deployed are sent out and arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The CIA sends out its men to do a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceman is slang for a cold-blooded professional assassin or hitman.

clue.text: Firm sauce served up for cat

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is put upward, read backwards

parts.note: ragu is an Italian meat sauce

explanation.surface: A firm sauce is dished out for the cat's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as an adjective for the sauce, but it is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar, or puma, is a large wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Bewildered foe abducts bats

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A confused onlooker sees an enemy carrying off some bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals being abducted, but it is the adjective for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obfuscated means confused or made obscure, so a muddled, befuddled state.

clue.text: Bottom surface in stiff loo roll

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words stiff loo roll

explanation.surface: Complaint about a scratchy toilet roll used on one's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' joins the loo roll joke, but the definition is the lowest surface of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor is the lowest surface of a room, the one people walk on.

clue.text: Noisily wear out part of car

indicators.note: noisily means spoken out loud, so the word is chosen for how it sounds

parts.note: to tire is to wear out

explanation.surface: Loud driving wears out part of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE is said aloud; the British spelling for the wheel part is TYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the rubber covering round a car's wheel.

clue.text: Bass cello regularly left in ring

parts.note: B is the music abbreviation for bass

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of cello

explanation.surface: A bass cello is left in a circle of players.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of cello gives EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is a ring in British slang, as in give someone a bell, a phone call.

clue.text: Try very large European bird

parts.note: a go is a try
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a very large European bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose is a large waterbird related to ducks and swans.

clue.text: Meadows outside of Edinburgh with ancient tenure

parts.note: leas are meadows

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: Meadows on the edge of Edinburgh have been held since ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Meadows is a real park in Edinburgh, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is a form of tenure, holding property under a lease for a fixed term.

clue.text: Artist at Royal Institute draws unusual objects

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
RI is the abbreviation for Royal Institute
ties are draws in sport

explanation.surface: A painter at the Royal Institute sketches odd objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws' reads as sketching, but it is the noun, drawn games.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarities are rare things, items seldom found.

clue.text: Tobogganist perhaps starting to sprint to top and show hesitation

indicators.note: the start of sprint is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of sprint
a lid is a top
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A tobogganist sprints off at the start, then dithers at the top of the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A slider is anyone who slides, and a tobogganist slides downhill, so is an example.
